t: You're at Paultons Square, a Georgian terraced garden square in Chelsea. It was built between 1836 and 1840 on the site of a former market garden, on land once owned by Sir Thomas More and Sir John Danvers. In the middle is a lawn behind metal railings, and the houses around it are all listed Grade Two. The architect and writer Katherine Shonfield lived here. She wrote regularly for Building Design and the Architects' Journal, and she was a founding member of muf architecture and art in 1994.
